text:
tara: quick sync - we need to pick a default for control-plane APIs powering Console (routing rules, quota checks, rollout commands). options: proto/gRPC internally, or plain REST/JSON everywhere. thoughts?

noah: personally prefer gRPC inside the mesh. proto gives strong typing and faster wire. streaming is handy for rollout progress updates.

zhen: +1 for typed contracts but ops loves curlability. if everything is gRPC we should provide a thin JSON facade for humans.

tara: agree. envoy grpc_json_transcoder can translate JSON to proto at the gateway. keeps internal services proto-first.

noah: two red flags: 1) header/span propagation across the gateway during transcoding; 2) quota attribution when one HTTP request fans out to multiple RPCs.

zhen: for tracing, ensure gateway forwards traceparent and we tag spans with a Console-op id. add a mandatory "x-console-op-id" header for all Console-originated requests.

tara: for quotas the Console needs per-route cost breakdowns. proposal: gateway emits "x-internal-op-attrib" listing sub-op ids and estimated token usage; billing ingests that.

alexa: ci-bot: FYI there's a canary slot open for gateway-transcode pool on 04/02 03:00 UTC. label: canary/transcode.

noah: perf question: JSON<->proto CPU overhead at scale. we should run a small POC with policy payloads (~15-30kb) and batch rollout lists.

zhen: also add tests for enum stability so dashboard labels don't change after proto updates. recommend proto CI generate JSON samples and compare names.

tara: UX ask from Console: show "estimated cost delta" inline when editing routing rules. backend can compute approximate token impact; no need to expose raw op ids.

noah: action items: 1) zhen to run JSON->proto perf POC and proto->json enum test; 2) tara to draft RFC (hybrid-proto-external-json.md) with envoy snippet and header formats; 3) noah to sketch quota attribution header format and idempotency rules.

zhen: will drop POC branch today and post perf numbers.
